title: Slip stitch
subtitle: An almost-invisible stitch for closing seams and attaching lining inside finished needlework.
excerpt: Slip stitch closes a turned seam or attaches a lining with barely a thread showing on the right side. It is worked by catching the fold of one fabric and a thread or two of the other alternately.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Joining stitches and lining application.
Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746. Slip stitch method.

glossaryTerms.definition: A nearly invisible stitch formed by alternately catching a few threads of one fabric and slipping through the fold of the other. Used to close openings and attach linings without visible stitching on the right side.

content.text: joins two folded fabric edges with almost no visible thread on either surface. It is used to close the opening in a finished needlework cushion, to attach backing fabric to a framed piece, or to join a hem edge to the front of a project.
Fold the seam allowance under on both pieces and align the folds face to face.
Anchor the thread with a small knot hidden inside the fold at one end.
Slip the needle along inside the fold of the front fabric for about 5 mm, then emerge at the fold edge.
Cross to the opposite fold and pick up 2 or 3 threads, then slip along inside that fold for 5 mm.
Continue alternating between the two folds. The thread between them is almost invisible when the seam is gently pulled closed.

items.symptom: The stitching shows on the right side
items.cause: The needle picked up fabric on the right side instead of slipping inside the fold.
items.fix: The needle must travel inside the fold, not through it. Approach at a very shallow angle.

items.symptom: The seam puckers when pulled closed
items.fix: Leave the thread slightly loose between stitches. Pull up after every 5 or 6 stitches, not after every individual stitch.

content.text: Slip stitch is essential for finishing needlework cushions, pincushions, and any project where an opening must be closed cleanly after the piece is turned.
is also used to attach the backing of a finished tapestry or Hardanger piece.
